messages.subject: Re: Error in R using test_all for merMod Objects
parts:
Hi Jim, and thank you for your message. Thank you too for the reproducible example. Part of why we didn't catch this error before was that we were using the sleepstudy data (built-in to lme4), which only has one predictor variable! Thanks again.
We just pushed an update which I believe fixes the bug. Could you install the development version (i.e., via devtools::install_github("jrosen48/konfound")) and let us know that it worked?
We also added a test--and added an acknowledgement in the news file for the next release (to J Murphy). If you would prefer we don't include your name in the news file, please let us know and we'll remove that.
-Josh






On Mon, Jan 28, 2019 at 1:13 AM Jim Murphy <jpc.m...@gmail.com> wrote:
I'm trying to work with the konfound R library using mixed effects objects (from lme4). I'm encountering an error when setting test_all=TRUE. (Different errors depending on whether one also includes or omits something for the tested_variable parameter.) The equivalent syntax for the exquivalent lm() models work fine.

The errors are below with a reproducible examples, both those that work and those that don't. Thanks in advance for your help.

library(konfound)
library(lme4)
library(mice)   #for example multivariate multilevel data popmis

data(popmis) #example data from mice

#as hlm (1a works; 1b and 1c do not)
testmod1 <- lmer(teachpop ~ texp + sex + (1| school), data=popmis)
testkon1a <- konfound(testmod1, texp, to_return = "raw_output")
Note that the Kenward-Roger approximation is used to estimate degrees of freedom for the predictor(s) of interest.

testkon1b <- konfound(testmod1, texp, test_all=TRUE, to_return = "raw_output")
Error in if (abs(obs_r) > abs(critical_r)) { : 
  missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed
In addition: Warning message:
In data.frame(t = est_eff/std_err, df = df_kr) :
  row names were found from a short variable and have been discarded

testkon1c <- konfound(testmod1, test_all=TRUE, to_return = "raw_output")
Error in data.frame(t = est_eff/std_err, df = df_kr) : 
  arguments imply differing number of rows: 4, 0

#as ols (all work)
testmod2 <- lm(teachpop ~ texp + sex, data=popmis)
testkon2a <- konfound(testmod2, texp, to_return = "raw_output")
Note that this output is calculated based on the correlation-based approach used in mkonfound()

testkon2b <- konfound(testmod2, texp, test_all=TRUE, to_return = "raw_output")
testkon2c <- konfound(testmod2, test_all=TRUE, to_return = "raw_output")

messages.subject: Re: Error in R using test_all for merMod Objects
parts:
Hi Josh:

Thanks for the quick fix. And sorry for the long delayed response. Before including (4a) below, I felt I should revisit the foundational articles.

My apologies in advance for the length. Please take your time.

(1) The new version works for the toy example, but it would be nice to have the variable name appear in the left column. There's no variable name right now. Here's what I get:

as.data.frame(testkon1b)
         t         df        action   inference pct_bias_to_change_inference  itcv r_con
1 6.532027   98.02971 to_invalidate reject_null                       64.313 0.441 0.664
2 8.827535 1904.15852 to_invalidate reject_null                       77.356 0.161 0.401

(2) While it works for the toy example, when I go to my actual application (which, unfortunately, I can't share with you for security reasons), I can't run konfound() on large lmer objects. 

Error in asMethod(object) :
  Choldmod_error 'problem too large' at file ../Core/cholmod_dense.c, line 105

The merMob object in question isn't particularly big. It's 7.7MB (roughly 50K observations from Add Health). konfound does work on the equivalent lm() object, which is much larger (14.4 mb).

(3) I found a really minor error in the source code for konfound-lm(). The warning message "Note that this output is calculated based on the correlation-based approach used in mkonfound()"  appears when test_all=FALSE. mkonfound() is actually run when when test_all=TRUE.

(4) This is more of a substantive question. I noticed that for a given covariate X, different results are produced depending on whether one uses konfound(DF, X) or konfound(DF, test_all=TRUE). Presumably that's because test_all=TRUE sends the model to mkonfound().

(a) Is there a formal description of the meta-analysis approach somewhere? I could only find brief mentions of it in the methodological articles and I would like to understand the divergent results. I see the gestures towards it in the 2003 Soc. Meth. article but I'm having trouble piecing the whole puzzle together.

(b) For a set of covariates where one wants to treat some as the focal causal variables of interest and some as "controls," is it better practice to (1) run the regular, non-meta-analysis version of konfound() separately for each potential causal variable, (2) run konfound using test_all=TRUE and get results for all variables in the model, or (3) create one's own data frame from scratch including just the focal causal variables' estimates and apply mkonfound()directly?

(And I would be flattered to receive an acknowledgment with the package.)

Jim
